mentions.text: Almost everyone will say they're huge music fans, enjoying music is probably one of the most common shared human experiences. But in there are vastly different levels of how "into it" people really are. Now obviously this is true for a lot of things, where there are casual fans and people who are more into it as a serious hobby. But for music there is a significant amount of people who will say that they're huge music fans that in reality have extremely shallow knowledge of the music scene, even of the artist that they're fans of. "I'm a huge country fan Chris Stapleton is my favorite singer" you ask what they thought of his latest album from the other year and get back a " Oh I don't know but Tennessee Whiskey is my favorite song." It's the people who used to mostly just put on top 40 radio, who now probably just have 5 or 6 spotify or youtube algorithm curated playlists saved that they listen on repeat. mentions.text: If we're using the example of jazz song about watering plants, then I may perhaps consider that devoid of effort. I think my opinion is fluid when it comes to prompt related assistance vs effort. It depends on the variables involved. I actually entered the jazz/plants prompt just now. While it generates a somewhat viable song, the song is muddy, unexpectedly drops and raises the gain, starts clipping and colliding with the kick, and has pitch issues with the vocals. Correcting these is where the talent and effort come into play, and that's where I disagree on the broad assertion that it's devoid of those. That's just my opinion today, so that could change as the models get better. As far as it being the majority of what is produced, I don't have the data on that, but my anecdotal experience on Spotify does not fall into that category. The songs recommended to me are usually of higher quality.
